Subject: MSA & Order Form: term/renewal redlines and termination-for-convenience language

Hi Claire —

Thanks again for the time today. Attached are the two documents we discussed (MSA v3 with inline redlines, and the Order Form PDF). Quick summary of the open items we flagged on call:

- Auto-renew term and renewal notice window (Customer asked for 30 days; current draft is 60).
- Term length and optional evergreen renewals for annual commitments.
- Termination for convenience (TFC) fee / ramp-down obligations and timing.
- Data export/handback SLA on termination (timeboxed).

From Redwood's perspective our negotiating priorities are: keep a 60-day notice window for auto-renew to allow capacity planning for Dedicated seats, limit TFC liability to 60 days of remaining committed fees for Multi-year deals, and preserve a right to provide transition support at our published professional services rates rather than an assumed fixed TFC fee.

Can you confirm StratusCloud's internal appetite for: (A) moving the notice window to 45 days as a compromise, or (B) if they require 30 days, accept the 60-day billing cap on TFC? If you prefer, we can sketch both options in the Order Form so legal has concrete language to redline.

Attachments: MSA_Stratus_v3_redline.docx (inline suggestions), OrderForm_Stratus_2027-02.pdf

Thanks — happy to set a short call to resolve the three bullet points.

Best,
Naomi Feldman

Hi Naomi —

Thanks for sending these over and for outlining Redwood's preferred positions. Quick responses from our side:

- Notice window: Stratus prefers 30 days for commercial flexibility across pilots and annual pilots, but we can consider 45 days if Redwood can accept a narrower TFC liability.
- TFC: We understand Redwood's operational concerns; Stratus is pushing for a pro-rata refund rather than a capped amount, plus a short handback SLA (30 days).
- Data handback: 30-day extraction period is fine; we can live with your standard export format.

I asked our legal team to review the inline redlines (copied legal@). They asked if you can provide alternative clause language for both: (1) a 30-day notice + pro-rata TFC, and (2) a 45-day notice + capped TFC equal to 60 days of fees. Having both options will speed approvals.

If you're available Monday morning we can do a 30-min call with legal to close on language.

Thanks,
Claire
Director, Procurement & Cloud Partnerships
StratusCloud

Hi Naomi / Karthik —

Thanks for the context and the clear option framing. Attached are proposed redlines (document: MSA_Stratus_v3_redline.docx). High-level notes below — I included exact clause language you can drop into the MSA and a brief Order Form note.

Option A (Stratus-preferred) — 30-day notice + pro-rata TFC
- Suggested MSA language: "Either Party may elect not to renew the Subscription by providing written notice at least thirty (30) days prior to the then-current term end date. If Customer terminates the Agreement for convenience prior to the end of a paid term, Customer shall be entitled to a pro-rata credit for unused prepaid fees calculated on a daily basis. Provider shall have thirty (30) days to provide Customer data export in Provider's standard formats."
- Commercial impact: higher variability in capacity planning; acceptable if Sales accepts potential elasticity risk.

Option B (Compromise) — 45-day notice + capped TFC
- Suggested MSA language: "Either Party may elect not to renew the Subscription by providing written notice at least forty-five (45) days prior to the then-current term end date. If Customer terminates the Agreement for convenience prior to the end of a paid term, Provider's aggregate liability for termination for convenience shall be limited to an amount equal to sixty (60) days of fees then in effect for the cancelled subscription. Provider shall offer up to thirty (30) days of transition support at Provider's then-current professional services rates. Provider shall provide Customer data export within thirty (30) days."
- Commercial impact: reduces provider exposure while shortening notice compromise for Customer. Sales can accept capped liability at 60 days for standard order sizes; exceptions (TCV > $1.5M) will require approval.

Order Form note (to appear under Termination & Renewal table): "Customer selects Option A (30-day notice / pro-rata refund) or Option B (45-day notice / capped 60-day TFC liability) as indicated below. For deals where Order Form Total Contract Value exceeds $1,500,000, Provider approval is required to accept Option A."

Next steps:
- Naomi: please confirm whether Stratus intends to pursue Option A or B after you speak with Claire on Monday.
- Karthik: please flag any strategic exceptions before we send the clean redline.

I can join the Monday call if helpful — otherwise happy to finalize redlines once Naomi confirms their preference.

Regards,
Marissa Cole
Senior Counsel | Redwood Inference
